about.title: Personal Injury Help in Atherton, California
about.longDescription: Atherton is a quiet community, but its roads still see their share of collisions. Public records show 3 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, with 3 people hurt and no traffic deaths reported. Reported crashes here tend to cluster on Wednesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., and the corridors with the highest collision counts include Middlefield Road, Route 82 (El Camino Real corridor), Alameda De Las Pulgas, and El Camino Real itself — all roads local residents use daily for errands, school runs, and commutes. If you were hurt in a crash on one of these streets, or anywhere else in town, sorting out medical bills, insurance calls, and missed work can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free connection service — we are not a law firm, and we don't handle your case ourselves. Instead, we help you connect with an independent personal injury attorney in our network who can look at what happened and explain your options. Attorneys we connect you with work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Reaching out costs nothing and starts the conversation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity is involved. Waiting too long can cost you the chance to recover anything at all.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help sort out how fault actually breaks down.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California doesn't limit how much you can recover for non-economic harm like pain and suffering. That means your compensation isn't artificially capped just because your losses go beyond medical bills.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they win or settle your case. That structure lets you get legal help without worrying about hourly rates or retainers.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Atherton?
items.answer: In most California injury cases, you have two years from the date of the incident to file a lawsuit. If your injury involved a government entity or public property, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for what happened. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated entirely.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Atherton?
items.answer: Public crash records show the highest collision counts on Middlefield Road, Route 82, Alameda De Las Pulgas, and El Camino Real. These are simply the corridors with the most reported incidents in recent data, not a judgment about any particular stretch of road.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys — we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover money.

items.question: Is there a cap on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In ordinary California injury cases, there's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. An attorney can help you understand what factors might affect the value of your specific claim.
